extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in analytic number theory / readers of Math Reviews
extracted.subtask_description: A Math Reviews style summary and commentary of Yitang Zhang's 2014 Annals paper proving bounded gaps between primes, describing the main theorem, hypotheses used (distributional hypotheses, admissible k-tuples), weights/sieve choices, and subsequent improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissibility of k-tuple H
rubrics_metrics.description: If νp(H) < p for all primes p, we say that H is admissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admissibility means the k-tuple H = {h1 < · · · < hk} does not occupy all residue classes modulo any prime p. The prime k-tuple conjecture asserts that every admissible H produces infinitely many n with n+hi all prime; admissibility is the basic combinatorial constraint needed to expect prime tuples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zhang's main theorem hypothesis (large k admissible tuple)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose that H is admissible with k ≥ 3.5 × 10^6. Then there are infinitely many positive integers n such that the set {n + h1, ..., n + hk} contains at least two primes; consequently lim inf_{n→∞}(p_{n+1} − p_n) < 7 × 10^7.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The theorem requires an admissible tuple H and a concrete lower bound on k; this explicit (but large) k is what produces Zhang's unconditional finite bound on prime gaps. Zhang himself notes the result is not optimal and subsequent work reduced these constants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level of distribution θ (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: We say that the primes have level of distribution θ if for any ε > 0, sum_{q ≤ N^{θ−ε}} max_{(a,q)=1} | sum_{p ≤ N, p ≡ a (mod q)} log p − N/φ(q) | = O(N (log N)^{-A}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This precise quantitative notion measures how well primes are equidistributed in arithmetic progressions on average over moduli up to N^{θ−ε}. It is a central hypothesis in relating sieve weights to small gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bombieri–Vinogradov as unconditional baseline (θ = 1/2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unconditionally, we know that the primes have level of distribution 1/2; this is the Bombieri–Vinogradov Theorem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bombieri–Vinogradov provides the standard unconditional distributional input for sieve-based small-gap arguments. Results that require θ > 1/2 are therefore conditional beyond current unconditional theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elliott–Halberstam conjecture (θ = 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: P. D. T. A. Elliott and H. Halberstam conjectured that the primes have level of distribution 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under Elliott–Halberstam (θ≈1) the Goldston–Pintz–Yıldırım method can produce very small k (e.g., k = 6) leading to explicit small gap bounds (example given: admissible set {7,11,13,17,19,23} gives lim inf gap ≤ 16). This conjecture therefore serves as a strong conditional hypothesis enabling much stronger conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: G P Y conditional implication for k (if θ > 1/2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Goldston, Pintz, and Yıldırım proved that if the primes have a level of distribution θ > 1/2, then there exists an explicitly calculable constant C(θ) depending only on θ such that for any admissible k-tuple H with k ≥ C(θ), the set {n + h1, ..., n + hk} contains at least two primes infinitely often.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives the conditional pathway from distributional strength to bounded gaps: better level of distribution (θ) lowers the required tuple size k. It explains why achieving θ > 1/2 (or assuming it) is powerful for small-gap results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction to smooth d / smooth moduli (Motohashi–Pintz observation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Motohashi and Pintz observed that the results are not materially changed if one restricts the ΛR-sum to smooth d (values of d with no large prime divisors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Zhang crucially uses this observation: by restricting to smooth moduli, one can limit attention to moduli for which the necessary equidistribution/estimates are tractable. It justifies focusing estimates on smooth q and applying the Chinese Remainder Theorem before dispersion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Selberg-type weights Λ_R(n; H)
rubrics_metrics.description: ΛR(n; H) is a sum of the form sum_{d | (n+h1)...(n+hk)} λ_d, motivated by the weights in the usual Selberg sieve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choosing suitable sieve weights ΛR is central: the sum over n of (sum_i θ(n+hi) − log 3N) ΛR(n; H)^2 is the quantity analyzed. Zhang (and earlier GPY) choose ΛR to mimic Selberg weights; Maynard later uses a multi-dimensional weight ΛR(n; H) = sum_{d1,...,dk} λ_{d1,...,dk} with different combinatorial structure, yielding alternate bounds and weaker distributional hypotheses (only Bombieri–Vinogradov).

rubrics_metrics.name: Chinese Remainder + estimates adequate for smooth moduli
rubrics_metrics.description: Zhang's approach is to apply the Chinese Remainder Theorem before opening the dispersion. The estimates are adequate only for smooth moduli, but this is sufficient because of the Motohashi–Pintz observation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The combination of CRT and restriction to smooth moduli allows control of residue-class counts even when q is composite and residue classes a can become large; this technical strategy is a key methodological criterion for Zhang's unconditional bound.
